title: HNSW and approximate nearest neighbour search
summary: A graph index that finds near-neighbours in a vector space quickly by walking a hierarchy of links, trading exactness for speed.
what: HNSW builds a layered graph where each vector links to its neighbours. Search enters at a sparse top layer, greedily walks toward the query, then descends to denser layers to refine.
why: Exact nearest-neighbour search compares the query to every vector. At 51,310 chunks that is tolerable; at ten million it is not. HNSW turns a linear scan into a graph walk.
how: Two knobs matter. m is how many links each node keeps, fixed at build time. ef_search is how many candidates the search keeps in flight, set per query — larger means more of the graph explored, better recall, more time.
in_this_project: Built in PostgreSQL via pgvector 0.8.6 with m=16, ef_construction=64. On the real corpus the index builds in about 8 seconds. Measured here: at the default ef_search=40 an unrestricted role recovers 0.850 of what exact search returns — approximate means approximate, and 15% is lost before access control is even involved.

formula.notation:
recall@k = |ANN top-k  n  exact top-k| / k

Measured on this corpus, unrestricted:
  ef_search=40   -> 0.850
  ef_search=100  -> 0.942
  ef_search=200  -> 0.967
  ef_search=800  -> 0.975

terms.meaning: links per node, fixed at build; higher is better recall and a larger index
candidate list size while building; higher is a better graph and a slower build
candidate list size while querying; the runtime recall/latency dial

advantages: ef_search tunable per query without rebuilding
limitations: Approximate by construction — recall is never 1.0 at practical settings
Build is not deterministic, so figures move between runs
Index is roughly twice the size of the raw vectors

pitfalls: Assuming ANN results equal exact results
Benchmarking at ef_search=40 and reporting it as retrieval quality
Filtering after the index has already chosen — see ANN post-filtering

use: Corpora large enough that exact scan is too slow
avoid: Small corpora where exact search is fast and exactly right
